positive_controls.argument: Observation of the real task, triangulated with configuration-linked traces and worker accounts, can reveal which condition the proposed verification method must discriminate and whether it can be observed in practice.
Provenance-bearing observations and traces can expose a discrepancy between a locally reported pass and actual integration behavior, supplying a bounded cross-level evidence item.
Actual-work observation and affected-user testimony can expose an unrecorded workaround or mismatch between the intended task and the formal workflow, changing the validation question.
Triangulated records and observations can identify a difference between the article actually tested and the representative article or envelope claimed, narrowing the credit.
Traced observations of the delivered item can corroborate or contradict a delivery report and expose an unresolved condition for the real acceptance decision.
Provenance-bearing observation can supply a bounded item under the actually applicable accepted means, while distinguishing what was seen from inferred compliance.
Accessible provenance and discrepancies across evidence channels give a competent challenger a concrete premise to inspect instead of relying only on managerial accounts.

Observed workarounds and corroborating traces can reveal that a stated control is bypassed or that the operational context differs from the hazard model, creating a bounded defeater or missing premise.
Triangulated observations with explicit provenance can support or defeat one claim premise while keeping observation separate from causal inference.
Observation of representative rehearsal, corroborated with configuration and event records, can expose an unplanned manual dependency or impossible handoff before reliance at cutover.
Periodic contextual observation and triangulation can identify a gap between automated evidence and the real work, requiring targeted interpretation or collection changes.
Triangulated observations can disclose an unrecorded exposure, burden or control limitation for the responsible decision-maker without supplying authority or an acceptable-risk criterion.
